newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan seeks charges in nuclear accident cover-up.
newsitem.headline: Japan seeks charges in nuclear accident cover-up.

text.p: The Japanese government formally asked police on Wednesday to press charges against a state-run firm over a cover-up in its handling of the nation's worst nuclear accident.

The government's Science and Technology Agency said it had filed a complaint with police against the state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) and several senior company officials, urging police to pursue legal action over the accident last month at a nuclear reprocessing plant.
PNC officials admitted last week they had lied about the procedures officials followed in dealing with a fire at the plant that triggered an explosion and radiation leak.

The report said staff made visual checks that the flames had been doused but in reality no such checks were made. The fire flared up again, causing an explosion at a bituminisation facility inside the PNC's reprocessing complex in Tokaimura, 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Tokyo.
Such a formal complaint with police or prosecutors is the first step in bringing charges against a person or institution.

The move coincided with fresh controversy about management lapses at the PNC after it emerged that the firm waited 30 hours before informing authorities of another radiation leak at a different nuclear plant on Monday. The PNC insisted the latest leak was minor and caused no damage.

In the more serious explosion on March 11, 37 workers were exposed to low levels of radiation. The accident was the nation's worst nuclear accident on record and heightened public anxiety about the safety of Japan's ambitious nuclear power programme -- a pillar of its energy policy.
If convicted of violating the law governing the operation of nuclear reactors, the PNC officials would face a fine of up to 200,000 yen ($1,587) each and a jail term of up to six months. ($1=126 yen)
